Container.Name: nuvira-server
Container.Overview: Your own server for NuviraHub, the self-hosted remote desktop and remote support app for Windows, macOS and Linux (open source, AGPL-3.0).[br][br] It handles signalling, the relay for devices that cannot connect directly, and the signed updates of the apps. Sessions are end-to-end encrypted between the two devices: the server never sees screen, input, clipboard or files.[br][br] In the NuviraHub app, enter this server's address in Settings → Server. A single port, 21116 UDP (plus TCP for the WebSocket fallback). Server address books, accounts, web console and the other team features are in the Pro edition (nuvira-server-pro).
Container.Requires: Forward port 21116 UDP (and TCP for the WebSocket fallback) from the router to Unraid, to reach the server from outside your network. Back up the Data folder: it holds the server's identity, which the apps pin.

Config.Name: Port (UDP)
Config.Description: Signalling and relay (QUIC). Forward it on the router.

Config.Name: Port (TCP)
Config.Description: WebSocket fallback for networks that block UDP, and app updates. Forward it on the router.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database, server certificate, and the app updates you publish to your devices: extract the nuvira-update zip of a release into the updates folder (its folders and .json files go straight in it). Back up the whole folder.

Config.Name: WebSocket listen
Config.Description: TCP address of the WebSocket fallback; off to disable it.

Config.Name: Limits per address
Config.Description: Limits on registrations and connection requests per address (local addresses are always exempt); off to disable them.
